Every :class:`CustomerType` plus ``ALL``. Kept separate from
:class:`CustomerType` because ``ALL`` is a question a caller can ask, never a
value a customer row can hold.

``COMMERCIAL`` is the default on every list, so a customer that cannot be
billed never reaches a picker asking "which commercial party is this". ``ALL``
is for the surfaces that administer the ``parent_customer`` hierarchy rather
than choose a payer.

Generate and download a daily report for a service order line.

Access is scoped to the authenticated user's customer projects.
If date is omitted, the report covers all activity dates for the SOL.

``require_content=False`` — the deliberate opt-out from the empty-day refusal
the internal surfaces take. ``date`` may be omitted here, so "empty" means
"this line has no activity at all", not "nothing happened that day"; the
caller is a portal in another repository whose 4xx handling we cannot see;
and there is no dialog here to show a message in. A customer asking for a
quiet line gets the quiet PDF rather than an error.

post.summary: Download a final (SOL) report — engine-rendered or uploaded
post.description:
Download the final report for a service order line, whatever its type.

The single final-report entry point for the portal — callers do not need to
know how a given service's report is produced. Every family renders on
demand, LER included: the render owns the final report, and a LER SOL only
falls back to the document ops uploaded when Ops Hub itself refuses to
render — the grid is not composed yet, or the service has no push builder
at all (``LER-TR`` / ``LER-TOP``).
That refusal is one dedicated exception, and it is the only thing this
catches. A reporting-engine failure reaches the same call as a plain
``ValidationError`` (``reports.client._execute_definition`` turns an
outage, a rejected token and a missing definition alike into one), and
answering that with the fallback would hand the customer whatever
unrelated document the line carries — labelled as their final report, 200
OK — every time the engine was down. The fallback streams the document
from storage the way ``core.endpoints.files`` serves stored files (GCS blob
bytes with the blob's own content type, falling back to a public-URL
redirect). Either way the response is the file bytes with a download
``Content-Disposition``, so the client handles one shape. A response is not
necessarily a PDF: an uploaded LER report may be a DOCX/XLSX/ZIP, and its
``Content-Type`` says so.

The customer-facing counterpart of the technician ``final-report/download``
endpoint (AECP-303): access is scoped to the caller's customer purely by
PostgreSQL RLS on ``ServiceOrderLine`` (via ``ServiceOrderHeader.customer_id``)
— a SOL the caller cannot see is not found, and that gate stays ahead of
every branch. The LER family is resolved ahead of the LPS branch here for
the same reason ``reports.api.render_final_report`` resolves it ahead of
its own cascade — one line must not resolve to two different families on
two routes, and this is the route where that costs most, because a client
reads what it returns. The exposure is smaller than on the technician
routes (this LPS check reads ``Service.group``, an FK, not the free-typed
``service_code``, so a stale code cannot reach it), but the order is the
invariant, not the size of today's hole. A refusal is a document fallback
only for LER: applied to any other family it would hand back whatever
unrelated document happens to be attached
(``_get_sol_uploaded_final_link`` matches *any* uploaded document once no
categorised one exists). Every other family's refusal reaches the customer
as a plain 404 — an LPS SOL with no project template among them, because
the technician-facing "Template not selected" message names an internal
setting ("Project Info") the portal's caller cannot act on.

get.summary: Download an uploaded final report file (e.g. LER)
get.description:
Download the uploaded final report attached to a service order line.

Deprecated in favour of ``POST /final``, which now serves uploaded finals
itself, so no client needs to classify the report type. Kept — and marked
deprecated in the schema rather than described as such in prose — for clients
pinned to the two-endpoint contract; it delegates to the same resolution
helpers, so the two cannot drift.

The customer-safe uploaded-file path (TD-1 / AECP-267). Ownership is
**verified, not assumed**: the SOL is resolved through the RLS-scoped
queryset first, so a SOL outside the caller's customer is invisible → 404,
and only then is its linked file served. This deliberately does **not** proxy
the generic ``/api/core/v1/files/service_order_line/{id}/`` endpoint, which
carries no customer RLS and no report permission.

The selection is resolved and refused here, before the engine is called: an id

type or stage, an empty result and an oversized selection are each a 422 naming
the cause.

Returns project rows (matched on project code or an active linked location

Matching is token-prefix and unicode-aware: the term must start the value

old "visible in the table, 403 on open" bug). Technician-group members
holding ``regular_user`` still only see their assigned projects, matching
the project list scope.

Provision Google Drive folders for a project if the ROOT link is not yet set.

Skips silently when the ROOT link already exists. Uses the Pipedrive deal URL
when available, then falls back to auto-discovery if it is missing or invalid.

Manually transition a project from Closure to Completed.

The cascade only advances projects up to Closure (all SOLs Completed or
Cancelled). Moving to Completed is an explicit close-out action — there
is no automatic trigger.

Manually set a project's status, bypassing the stage gates.

Privileged override gated behind the ``force_complete_project`` permission.
Any status except Cancelled can be set, in either direction, including
reopening a Completed project. Rules, audit trail, and the deliberate
no-side-effects contract live in ``ProjectManager.override_status``. The
automatic status rules (SOL cascade, nightly reconciler) stay active and
may later move the status again.

put.description:
Set or clear the customer pre-job questionnaire 'received' timestamp.

This is the Core replacement for the legacy ``PUT /projects/{id}/user-status``
pre-job workflow path. Only the *null-ness* of ``payload.pre_job_received_at``
is read — it signals intent; the timestamp itself is stamped **server-side**
(``timezone.now()``) to stay robust against client clock skew:

- ``null -> non-null`` (customer **submit**): stamps the timestamp, sends the
  pre-job submission notification, and re-runs the Pipedrive status cascade
  (advancing the project to Planning when probability is 100).
- ``non-null -> null`` (staff **reopen**): clears the timestamp; no email,
  no cascade.
- already-received re-submit: keeps the existing timestamp; no side effects.

get.description: List workorder activity metadata entries.

Return all data needed for the dispatching board.

Aggregates:
- Project resource sets with their members
- All project workorders (service + admin) with resource assignments
- Service order lines grouped for the panel

When both ``since`` and ``until`` are supplied, the workorders list is
filtered to a date window — useful for the dispatching console where
only the relevant working set should be returned. The five filter
clauses are: scheduled in window, mandatory in window,
assigned-but-unscheduled, due-dated backlog within
``dispatch.managers.board_reads.BACKLOG_HORIZON_DAYS``, and unassigned
WOs from PLANNING/EXECUTION projects (regardless of due date). Without
the params, the legacy behaviour is preserved (returns all non-cancelled
workorders).

The windowed result also folds in real work that was logged but never
formally dispatched (DISP-4368, see
``dispatch.managers.logged_unplanned._get_logged_unplanned_workorders``)
-- those rows carry ``is_logged_unplanned=True`` with a planned window
derived from the actual logged activity times, and are dropped entirely
if that derived window clashes with a genuinely planned entry for one of
the same resources.

get.description:
Per-turbine status + activity-group completion for the whole project,
regardless of the board's date window (see
``dispatch.managers.board_reads._get_project_turbines``).

Kept on its own query, decoupled from ``board-data``'s per-mutation
refetch cycle, since this scan covers every non-cancelled workorder in
the project and dominates payload size.

get.summary: Server-filtered, paginated work-order list for the dispatch sidebar
get.description:
Sidebar work-order list with server-side filtering and pagination.

A large project can hold thousands of unassigned workorders — shipping
them all inside ``board-data`` made the board slow and the browser
unstable, so the sidebar reads this endpoint instead (and ``board-data``
is called with ``include_backlog=false``).

Filters: ``q`` full-text-ish search (name, description, service code,
turbine name, SO number); ``assignment`` open|unassigned|assigned, where
``assigned`` means an active resource-set link EXISTS, ``unassigned`` means
none does, and ``open`` (the default, what the sidebar shows) is
unassigned work PLUS any ``IN_PROGRESS`` workorder regardless of its team
link -- running work that was dispatched earlier still has to be found
and moved to the next day when it does not finish, and it normally still
carries its team; ``statuses``/``kinds``/``service_codes`` as
comma-separated lists; ``logged_unplanned`` narrows to (``true``) or
excludes (``false``) real work logged with no formal dispatch (DISP-4368)
-- these rows are already part of the unassigned scope and otherwise
indistinguishable by status from any untouched backlog WO, so this is
what makes them findable across a project's full backlog rather than only
on whichever board day/week they happen to be scrolled to. ``counts`` in
the response carries facet totals for the filter chips, each computed
before its own facet filter (standard faceting), over the search +
assignment scope.

See ``dispatch.managers.backlog._get_backlog_sync`` for the query shape:
the assignment counts come from one query (grouping on a ``has_team``
annotation rather than filtering `base` twice), and the three facet
breakdowns (statuses/kinds/services) come from one grouped query across
all three dimensions at once, summed per dimension in Python.

Hourly weather forecast for a project location on ``date``.

The whole UTC day, read from the ``weather_forecast`` cache (kept warm by the scheduled Gust sync). On a
cache miss for an in-horizon day, the location's bucket is backfilled from
Gust on the fly (one query) and re-read. Fail-soft: returns
``available=false`` with no hours when the location has no coordinates or no
forecast is available, so the board always renders.

post.summary: Create an ADMIN workorder assigned to a single technician
post.description:
Create a standalone ADMIN workorder pinned to one individual technician.

The workorder is scoped to ``project_id`` and inherits the project's
``requesting_customer`` (so it is visible under the customer-scoped RLS
policy and returned by ``board-data``). It is created with
``type=ADMIN`` / ``status=NOT_STARTED`` via the canonical
``WorkorderManager.gql_create`` path, then linked to the project resource
set the technician belongs to and pinned to that individual — reusing the
same assignment machinery as ``/assign`` so the board routes it into the
member's person lane.

The manager creates, links, and pins the workorder inside one
transaction: if the resource-set or assignee step fails, the workorder
must not be left committed without its dispatch links (mirrors the
atomic pattern in ``_assign_workorders_bulk_sync``).

get.description:

Return all data needed for the dispatching board.

Aggregates:
- Project resource sets with their members
- All project workorders (service + admin) with resource assignments
- Service order lines grouped for the panel

When both ``since`` and ``until`` are supplied, the workorders list is
filtered to a date window — useful for the dispatching console where
only the relevant working set should be returned. The five filter
clauses are: scheduled in window, mandatory in window,
assigned-but-unscheduled, due-dated backlog within
``dispatch.managers.board_reads.BACKLOG_HORIZON_DAYS``, and unassigned
WOs from PLANNING/EXECUTION projects (regardless of due date). Without
the params, the legacy behaviour is preserved (returns all non-cancelled
workorders).

The windowed result also folds in real work that was logged but never
formally dispatched (DISP-4368, see
``dispatch.managers.logged_unplanned._get_logged_unplanned_workorders``)
-- those rows carry ``is_logged_unplanned=True`` with a planned window
derived from the actual logged activity times, and are dropped entirely
if that derived window clashes with a genuinely planned entry for one of
the same resources.

get.summary: Get per-turbine status rollup for the dispatching board

Per-turbine status + activity-group completion for the whole project,
regardless of the board's date window (see
``dispatch.managers.board_reads._get_project_turbines``).

Kept on its own query, decoupled from ``board-data``'s per-mutation
refetch cycle, since this scan covers every non-cancelled workorder in
the project and dominates payload size.

get.summary: Server-filtered, paginated work-order list for the dispatch sidebar
get.description:
Sidebar work-order list with server-side filtering and pagination.

A large project can hold thousands of unassigned workorders — shipping
them all inside ``board-data`` made the board slow and the browser
unstable, so the sidebar reads this endpoint instead (and ``board-data``
is called with ``include_backlog=false``).

Filters: ``q`` full-text-ish search (name, description, service code,
turbine name, SO number); ``assignment`` open|unassigned|assigned, where
``assigned`` means an active resource-set link EXISTS, ``unassigned`` means
none does, and ``open`` (the default, what the sidebar shows) is
unassigned work PLUS any ``IN_PROGRESS`` workorder regardless of its team
link -- running work that was dispatched earlier still has to be found
and moved to the next day when it does not finish, and it normally still
carries its team; ``statuses``/``kinds``/``service_codes`` as
comma-separated lists; ``logged_unplanned`` narrows to (``true``) or
excludes (``false``) real work logged with no formal dispatch (DISP-4368)
-- these rows are already part of the unassigned scope and otherwise
indistinguishable by status from any untouched backlog WO, so this is
what makes them findable across a project's full backlog rather than only
on whichever board day/week they happen to be scrolled to. ``counts`` in
the response carries facet totals for the filter chips, each computed
before its own facet filter (standard faceting), over the search +
assignment scope.

See ``dispatch.managers.backlog._get_backlog_sync`` for the query shape:
the assignment counts come from one query (grouping on a ``has_team``
annotation rather than filtering `base` twice), and the three facet
breakdowns (statuses/kinds/services) come from one grouped query across
all three dimensions at once, summed per dimension in Python.

Hourly weather forecast for a project location on ``date``.

The whole UTC day, read from the ``weather_forecast`` cache (kept warm by the scheduled Gust sync). On a
cache miss for an in-horizon day, the location's bucket is backfilled from
Gust on the fly (one query) and re-read. Fail-soft: returns
``available=false`` with no hours when the location has no coordinates or no
forecast is available, so the board always renders.

post.summary: Create an ADMIN workorder assigned to a single technician
post.description:
Create a standalone ADMIN workorder pinned to one individual technician.

The workorder is scoped to ``project_id`` and inherits the project's
``requesting_customer`` (so it is visible under the customer-scoped RLS
policy and returned by ``board-data``). It is created with
``type=ADMIN`` / ``status=NOT_STARTED`` via the canonical
``WorkorderManager.gql_create`` path, then linked to the project resource
set the technician belongs to and pinned to that individual — reusing the
same assignment machinery as ``/assign`` so the board routes it into the
member's person lane.

The manager creates, links, and pins the workorder inside one
transaction: if the resource-set or assignee step fails, the workorder
must not be left committed without its dispatch links (mirrors the
atomic pattern in ``_assign_workorders_bulk_sync``).

get.description:
Bulk rollup (SOL/WO stats, action queue, value coverage, turbine count) for
the given ``project_ids`` (comma-separated numeric ids), keyed by id.

Base project fields come from ``GET /api/core/v1/projects``; the frontend
merges this map into the card list by id. The requested ids are narrowed by
the same visibility rule as that list (``ProjectManager.visible_to``), so
every card the list shows gets a rollup — a board filtered to another PM's
projects included. Ids the caller may not read, deleted or unknown ids, and
malformed tokens are dropped silently rather than failing the batch.

``MAX_ROLLUP_PROJECT_IDS`` is an abuse bound, not a page size: it sits above
the number of projects that exist, so a whole board always fits in one call.
That matters because the MFE treats any non-200 as "endpoint absent" and
falls back to per-project assembly, so a limit a real board could hit would
re-create the request storm this endpoint removes. Matched rows and response
size still grow with the id count even though the query count does not.

post.description:
Approve every actionable slot of a TR — WMS-initiated team approval.

Mirrors the planner's per-slot approval, but for the whole TR at once.
The API key's user must hold ``approve_team_request_slot``; the approval
is attributed to that user in the activity log.

SUBMITTED → SENT_TO_PLANNER from the WMS certificate pre-check.

Optional JSON body ``{actor_name, actor_email}``, read by hand because an
empty body is valid. Idempotent: a TR past SUBMITTED answers 200 with
``changed: false``. CANCELLED is 409; ``ROBOT_SET_REMOVED`` /
``PRE_JOB_HAS_UNRESOLVED_CERTS`` are 422.

PEOPLE_ASSIGNED → TEAM_VERIFIED from the WMS certificate approval.

``slots`` is the team the controller checked, one ``{slot_id, resource_id}``
per bound seat. Idempotent on TEAM_VERIFIED (``changed: false``). 409 for
any other status, a team that changed since the check, or a rejected seat.
``actor_email`` is accepted for parity with ``/send-to-planner`` but unused.

Add and remove required certificates on a TR and its active slots.

The WMS certificate controller's per-card decision. Idempotent. 409 on a
CANCELLED TR, 422 when an id is in both lists. Unknown or retired ids are
listed under ``refused`` and not applied.

post.summary: Complete Work Orders (and cascade linked anomalies)
post.description:
Atomically complete each work order and advance its linked anomaly.

Productionises AECP-333 (pairs the portal's AECP-329 two-call orchestration):
per work order, in one transaction, set ``status=completed`` (stamping
``completed_date``) and — if it has a linked anomaly — advance that anomaly's
``stage`` -> ``RESOLUTION_COMPLETE`` (which recomputes ``resolution_status``
-> ``RESOLVED``). A WO with no anomaly completes with ``cascade="none"``; if a
WO's cascade fails, that WO rolls back (``cascade="failed"``) while the others
still succeed. Gated on work-management-manage; the cascade is RLS-scoped, so
it can only advance anomalies the caller's customer owns.

CustomerType.description:
What kind of party a customer row represents.

``COMMERCIAL`` is an ordinary customer: billable, mirrored to NetSuite, and the
answer every customer picker in the product is asking for.

``VIRTUAL`` is an organisation that exists only so a group of users can read
across the customers beneath it in the ``parent_customer`` tree. It is never
billed and never mirrored to NetSuite or Pipedrive.

The vocabulary lives here rather than in a database constraint, so adding a kind
stays a product decision and not a deploy-ordering problem.

A type carries no access meaning. Scope expansion is decided entirely by
``parent_customer`` and ``deleted_at`` in ``rls.tenant_scope``, which never reads
this column, so changing it neither grants nor revokes anything.

RepairMaterialResponse.description:
One repair product of the shared item catalogue.

The admin-maintained products a repair service picks a material from - the
rows of ``core.item`` that carry a ``material_type``. ``name`` is the
commercial name printed to a customer, never the purchasing description the
same row shows a Set Request. ``coating_system`` and ``aliases`` are how our
own data spells the product (service-item codes, AeroTask ``Material type``
values), not marketing synonyms; ``repair_width_per_shell_mm`` and
``lep_thickness_um`` are the product's specified application width and film
thickness, absent until somebody enters them.

``name`` and ``description`` read through a ``validation_alias`` because
both names mean something else on the model: ``core.item.description`` is
the purchasing label, carrying pack size and colour code, and this response
must never hand a customer that. The alias is what makes the projection
structural - the fields cannot silently start reading the column they are
named after.

A receptor is a ``TurbineComponent`` with ``component_type`` Receptor or
HV Receptor and ``parent_turbine_component`` set to the owning blade.
The sync endpoint operates on the receptor children of one blade at a
time.

Upsert by ``id``: rows with ``id`` set update the matching record; rows
without ``id`` create a new one. Existing rows whose ``id`` is omitted
from the list are soft-deleted (full-list sync semantics).

pair_index.description: 1 or 2 for paired receptors (turbine model has double_receptors / hv_double_receptors set); NULL for non-paired. The frontend echoes back what GET returned so paired rows round-trip through a full-list PUT; on update by id the value is preserved when omitted.
pair_index.title: Pair Index

LerLayout.description:
A blade's grid: phase COLUMNS x position ROWS.

Per blade, not per SOL: a report section prints one blade, so one blade
legitimately needs a filler pass the others did not. The client applies an
edit to every blade of the SOL by default, which is an input convenience,
not the storage shape.

Empty on an upsert means "no opinion" and leaves the stored layout alone.
LerLayout.title: LerLayout

LerLayoutEntry.description:
One axis entry of a blade's grid: a phase column or a position row.

``key`` is what lands in an image's ``additional_information`` and is
therefore permanent; ``label`` is display wording and may be edited. Custom
keys carry an axis prefix (``PH_`` / ``POS_``).

pinned.description: FIRST / LAST for the ends the report fixes (Before + After, Root + Tip). Derived on read and ignored on write — the order is validated against the same rule either way.
pinned.title: Pinned

auto.description: True when the key is not in the saved layout but data already uses it, so the grid cannot drop it without hiding an image.
auto.title: Auto

LerLayoutEntry.title: LerLayoutEntry

LerMaterial.description:
One material row on a blade (Filler / LEP / Topcoat / ...).

``uid`` is a stable client-generated identifier so material media
(FileEntityLink rows tagged ``ler_material_media``) survive row
reordering and renames. Temperatures are canonically Celsius — the FE
F/C toggle is display-only.

``expiration_date`` is FREE TEXT: it is trimmed and nothing else, which is
deliberate and is the one place this payload does not validate a date.
``service_date`` beside it is ours: the panel picks it and the upsert
answers 422 on anything but ISO. An expiry is not ours — it is copied off a
tin by a technician into an AeroTask custom field, so the column already
holds ``02/2027`` and ``see batch``. Parsing those would either drop a
value that is the only record of the expiry, or read ``01/05/2027``
month-first where the panel reads it day-first and silently change what a
customer deliverable prints. The panel reads it tolerantly instead
(``parseLerDate``), normalises to ISO whatever it can render in the picker,
and flags the rest as text.

``application`` names the AeroTask step a LER RAT 4-5 row was read from
("Topcoat Application L1, 2026-06-30"); grid lines merge a material's
applications into one row and leave it null.
LerMaterial.title: LerMaterial

LerMaterialPhoto.description:
One label photo of a material row, referenced from AeroTask.

``attachment_id`` is the id AS STORED, never coerced: an integer
``core.file.id`` and a UUID legacy storage id share the key, and the client
picks the download route from its shape. ``workorder_activity_id`` is the
activity the field was read from, which the integer route needs to build a
URL at all.

One entry per ``kind`` — the slot holds a single image. ``extra`` is how
many more attachments that field carried, so a technician who dropped
fifteen pictures into one label field is visible as a number instead of a
wall of thumbnails.
LerMaterialPhoto.title: LerMaterialPhoto

LerMaterialTypeOption.description:
A material the name dropdown offers, from the catalogue or from this SOL.

``value`` is the product name stored in ``material.name``; ``bucket`` is the
coarse ``MATERIAL_TYPE_OPTIONS`` value stored in ``material.material_type``.
They are separate so the product list can grow without widening the
validated ``material_type`` vocabulary.

``source`` separates two claims that must not be presented as one.
``"sol"`` means this SOL's own service items or workorder activities name
the product — evidence it was applied here. ``"catalogue"`` means it is one
of the products the LER Tribe supplies, offered so an operator picks a
spelling instead of inventing one; it says nothing about this repair. The
client groups by it rather than merging the two into one list.

``coating_system`` is the spelling this SOL's own data holds, and only a
``"sol"`` option carries one. The endpoints run with ``exclude_none=True``,
so a catalogue option has no such key at all — read it with ``.get()``.

``description`` is the catalogued product's own, written by an admin into
``core.item.material_description``. It describes the PRODUCT, never this
repair, and a product nobody has described has no such key either.
LerMaterialTypeOption.title: LerMaterialTypeOption

LerOverflowCell.description:
A grid cell holding more than the one image the report frame prints.

Uploads go through the shared files endpoint, which must not learn LER's
cardinality, so a surplus is made visible here instead of being prevented
there or silently hidden.
LerOverflowCell.title: LerOverflowCell

LerPhaseComposite.description:
A phase column that has been composed into a single stored image.

The FILE is not repeated here — it is already in the SOL's file list, and
returning it twice would create two places for one truth. ``recipe_hash``
IS here: it is not part of the file, it is the fingerprint this response was
computed against, and a rebuild has to echo it back as
``expected_recipe_hash``. Reading it out of the file's
``additional_information`` instead would make the client depend on a storage
format this API deliberately hides.

``is_fresh`` is recomputed from the RESOLVED grid on every read, not from
the placements as they were stored: VIS auto-fill moves an unpinned photo at
read time with no operator save at all. A stale composite does not print;
the column falls back to its individual frames until it is rebuilt.

current_recipe_hash.description: Hash of the column as the grid reads now; a discard echoes it back.
current_recipe_hash.title: Current Recipe Hash

blank_positions.description: Position keys this composed image prints as blank frames.
blank_positions.title: Blank Positions

changes.description: What moved since it was composed; empty when is_fresh.
changes.title: Changes

discard_blocker.description: Why Discard changes cannot put this stale column back; null when it can, and always null when is_fresh.

discard_file_ids.description: Uploaded photos Discard changes writes back; empty when is_fresh.
discard_file_ids.title: Discard File Ids

discard_vis_photo_ids.description: VIS photos Discard changes writes back; empty when is_fresh.
discard_vis_photo_ids.title: Discard Vis Photo Ids

LerPhaseComposite.title: LerPhaseComposite

LerPhaseCompositeChange.description:
One row of the difference between a composed column and the grid now.

``kind`` is a ``LerCompositeChangeKind`` value (SOURCE_REPLACED,
FRAMING_CHANGED, POSITION_ADDED, POSITION_REMOVED, MOVED). ``detail`` is the
sentence the rebuild dialog prints beside the row's label, and is absent
where the kind says everything.

``from_position`` accompanies MOVED and is the row the photo came from, as a
KEY. The label belongs to the blade's own grid, so the dialog resolves it
the way every other address on this screen is resolved; a key baked into
``detail`` would print ``moved from POS_3`` at the operator.
LerPhaseCompositeChange.title: LerPhaseCompositeChange

LerPhaseCompositeDiscardBlocker.description: Why a stale column cannot return to its composed state; ``position`` is a row KEY.
LerPhaseCompositeDiscardBlocker.title: LerPhaseCompositeDiscardBlocker

LerRepairDefaults.description:
Repair dimensions implied by one LEP product.

A LIST entry carrying its own ``material`` field rather than a map keyed by
the product name: the frontend's response interceptor camel-cases every
object KEY it walks, so a name-keyed map would arrive under a mangled key
and never match. (Same reason the dispatching backlog returns facet counts
as ``{key, count}`` rows.)
LerRepairDefaults.title: LerRepairDefaults

LerRepairInfo.description:

LerRepairInfo.title: LerRepairInfo

LerReportField.description:
One cell of the read-only report mirror (block B, Scope Of The Service).

A cell carries either ``value`` or ``missing``, never neither: a blank cell
in a mirror of a customer deliverable reads as a zero, and making the gaps
visible to DataOps is the reason the block exists.

``value`` is already the string the report prints. ``number`` is for a value
the client re-formats itself, so the conversion stays one function on the
client; no field of this block needs it today.

unit.description: Unit of the FIELD, never part of the value (the report prints MW for nominal power, which the database does not store).
unit.title: Unit

LerReportField.title: LerReportField

LerReportMissing.description:
Why a read-only report cell is empty: what it means, where, whose data.

Three parts on purpose. ``hint`` is the finished sentence the operator reads
first; ``field`` is the exact database address a developer needs once the UI
wording and the column have drifted apart; ``owner`` is who owes the value.
All three are composed on the backend, next to the code that decided the
value is absent, so the UI never assembles a sentence out of a key.

field.description: Exact database address, for a developer.
field.title: Field

LerImagePlacement.description:
Where one image sits: which cell, and how it is framed inside it.

Exactly one of ``file_id`` (an uploaded phase image) / ``vis_photo_id`` (a
VIS frame). An offset is the image centre's distance from the frame centre
in fractions of the FRAME's own size, over a ``cover`` base fit at
``scale = 1``; zooming out below 1 is legitimate and uncovers the template
background. Fractions of the frame's spare room, the first contract, break
at exactly that point: spare room is zero once the image no longer fills
the frame — see docs/ai/ler-service-results.md § Placement.

ProjectScopeChangeRequestCustomFieldsOut.description:
Read-side twin of the custom-fields schema — must never 500 a GET.

``custom_fields`` has no DB type constraint, so a legacy or
hand-written row can violate the input contract the strict parent
enforces on create. On serialization, malformed ids degrade to null
(mirroring the regex-guarded SQL annotations that resolve the same
keys), unknown keys are surfaced as-is instead of failing the
response model, and the condition sections loosen to bare dicts —
the strict nested schemas would fail a GET over a hand-written row,
and the UI parses the sections defensively anyway.

source_service_order_line_id.description: Source SOL id. Required when the scope change is a service replacement; must be paired with replacement_service_id.
source_service_order_line_id.title: Source Service Order Line Id

source_turbine_component_id.description: TurbineComponent (blade) id the change applies to. Only meaningful on a service replacement whose source SOL covers the whole turbine (no pinned component): only the chosen blade's workorders move to the new SOL, and the source SOL stays active for the other blades. Omit (or null) to change the whole turbine — the source SOL is cancelled as before. On a blade-pinned source SOL the field must be absent or equal the pinned component.
source_turbine_component_id.title: Source Turbine Component Id

replacement_service_id.description: Replacement service id. Required when the scope change is a service replacement; must be paired with source_service_order_line_id.
replacement_service_id.title: Replacement Service Id

evidence_file_ids.description: core.File ids of evidence files previously uploaded via POST /api/core/v1/files. The backend creates a FileEntityLink row per id in the same transaction as the SCR; unknown ids cause the whole create to roll back with 422. The ids also persist in this JSON column as the historical input contract.
evidence_file_ids.title: Evidence File Ids

additional_workorders.description: Persisted copy of the top-level create field of the same name. The backend writes it here so a request that awaits QC → Sales → PM review still knows which workorders to generate when the finalize cascade eventually runs (possibly days after creation). Read-only in practice — supply the top-level create field instead of writing this key directly.
additional_workorders.title: Additional Workorders

ProjectScopeChangeRequestCreate.description:
Schema for creating a project scope change.

The service-replacement linkage (``source_service_order_line_id`` and
``replacement_service_id``) and evidence file references
(``evidence_file_ids``) live inside ``custom_fields`` — the payload
mirrors DB structure rather than inventing top-level body keys for
fields that don't have dedicated columns. ``additional_workorders``
is a sibling top-level body property (the historical wire contract);
the backend persists it into ``custom_fields`` so a request awaiting
review still honors it at the deferred finalize.

additional_workorders.description: Optional follow-up generation step — service items from the replacement service to generate as NOT_STARTED workorders on the new SOL, each optionally narrowed to a subset of the source turbine's components. Strongly recommended; without this, the new SOL may end up at FIELD_COMPLETED right after the scope change because every migrated workorder is force-completed and no replacement-service work exists yet. Service item ids are validated at create time (must exist, be live, and belong to custom_fields.replacement_service_id — 422 otherwise). ProjectScopeChangeRequestUpdate.description:
Fields editable on a request that still awaits review.

Editable at any waiting stage (QC, Sales or PM) by a holder of any
review permission. APPROVED (the cascade ran) and REJECTED (terminal)
are immutable; correcting those means reject + recreate. The source
SOL and type are deliberately not editable: re-pointing the request at
a different line is a new request. ``replacement_service_id`` and
``additional_workorders`` live in ``custom_fields`` on the row; they
are top-level here so the editable surface stays an explicit whitelist.

description.description: Legacy free text; new clients edit what_changed.
description.title: Description

what_changed.description: What makes the request a scope change. Cannot be blank on a request whose replacement service is the source line's own service.
what_changed.title: What Changed

replacement_service_id.description: New replacement service (stored as custom_fields.replacement_service_id). Must be an LER service. When it changes, additional_workorders must be re-submitted in the same call — the previously selected service items belong to the old replacement service.
replacement_service_id.title: Replacement Service Id

additional_workorders.description: Replaces the persisted additional_workorders plan; validated against the (possibly new) replacement service. Pass an empty list to clear the plan.
additional_workorders.title: Additional Workorders

evidence_file_ids.description: Replaces the linked evidence set. Ids are diffed against the current set: newly added ids get a FileEntityLink row (pre-upload the binaries via POST /api/core/v1/files), removed ids get their link soft-deleted. The AeroTask minimum-evidence rule applies at create time only — the QC reviewer editing a request may remove all images.
evidence_file_ids.title: Evidence File Ids

initial_evaluation_condition.description: Replaces the stored initial-evaluation condition section (custom_fields.initial_evaluation_condition). Pass null to clear it; omit to leave it unchanged. Its image_file_ids are diffed into FileEntityLink rows like evidence_file_ids.

current_condition.description: Replaces the stored current-condition section (custom_fields.current_condition). Pass null to clear it; omit to leave it unchanged. Its image_file_ids are diffed into FileEntityLink rows like evidence_file_ids.

ProjectScopeChangeRequestUpdate.title: ProjectScopeChangeRequestUpdate

expected_status.description: The status the caller believes the request is in — an optimistic-concurrency token. Each call advances the state machine exactly one stage; a mismatch (double-click, racing reviewer, terminal status) yields 422 with zero side effects. The caller needs the approval permission of this stage.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the status change log entry.

name, else ``"Unknown"``. ``units`` counts every sold line for the

``ProjectOverviewScopeRollup.by_status``, so they always sum to at most

AdminActivityInput.description:

and "add an activity to an already-created one" (``add_workorder_activity``
below).

``estimated_duration_minutes`` stays optional here -- adding to an existing
WO has never required one -- but if given it must be a real, positive
number, never the old silent-zero default. Workorder *creation* additionally
requires every activity to carry one; see
``CreateAdminWorkorderPayload.validate_payload``.

``image_required`` (FEAT-2554) mirrors the ``custom_fields`` shape the
"Replace Cleaning Cloth" field activity already uses to require a photo
before AeroTask lets the activity complete (see migration

than inventing a second mechanism for the same thing.

CreateAdminWorkorderPayload.description:
Payload for creating an ADMIN workorder pinned to a single technician.

An admin workorder is standalone work (no service order line) scoped to the
currently-open project: it inherits the project's ``requesting_customer`` so
the row is visible under the customer-scoped RLS policy and returned by the
project ``board-data`` query. ``assignee_resource_id`` pins the WO to one
individual so the board routes it into that member's person lane; the
resource must belong to an active project resource set of this project.

``activities`` requires at least one entry -- AeroTask's start/finish/
update flow acts on WorkorderActivity rows, not bare workorders, so an
ADMIN WO with none is inert on mobile (DISP-2379). FEAT-2554 dropped the
free-text whole-WO ``description`` in favour of the Activities section
(which now always carries real, timed activities) and caps their combined
duration at the workorder's own -- both enforced below.

``auto_carry_over`` is opt-in (DISP-3391): while the workorder is
incomplete, the hourly carry-over task keeps shifting its planned window
onto the site's current day.
CreateAdminWorkorderPayload.title: CreateAdminWorkorderPayload

ResolveCertTokenPayload.description:
Body for POST /team-requests/{id}/resolve-cert-token.

The doc-controller picks one unresolved token and tells the server what to
do with it: ``map`` it to an existing Certificate or ``drop`` it (strip
with no new requirement). Certificates are never created here: they come
from the Roster sync.

The token is stripped from both pre-job cert answers — the
``required_certifications`` list and the free-text
``other_certification_details`` — across every site the TR spans. Matching
nothing is a 422, not a silent success.

ServiceRateItem.description:
One service rate row per service for the OPS_HUB sidebar.

A service can be priced by several CO lines (one per asset). Those lines are
collapsed into a single row: ``co_item_ids`` holds every contributing CO line
and ``rate`` is only set when they all agree on one price — otherwise it is
``None`` and the real rate is picked per asset in the charge-creation modal.
Material lines that belong to a service line are not collapsed across service
lines: each (service, ``parent_line_key``) pair gets its own row.

service_netsuite_id.description: NetSuite item id of the service — lets the frontend address the NS line item when it falls back to the legacy charge flow for services without scope items (EXTRA, MOB, ACC, ...)
service_netsuite_id.title: Service Netsuite Id

rate.description: Unit rate when every CO line for this service shares one price; None when they differ — the rate then comes from the asset's own CO line, chosen in the charge-creation modal
rate.title: Rate

co_item_ids.description: Every CO line item ID priced under this service — the modal resolves assets across all of them
co_item_ids.title: Co Item Ids

parent_line_key.description: line_key of the service line these material lines belong to
parent_line_key.title: Parent Line Key

parent_line_label.description: That service line's code and site on this offer, e.g. LER-3 · Polaris
parent_line_label.title: Parent Line Label

parent_service_id.description: Service of that service line, so the row nests under it
parent_service_id.title: Parent Service Id

ChargeSolSchema.description:
A completed SOL with no charge against it, as the action queue lists it.

Identification only. Raising the charge happens in the project's accounting
calendar, which resolves its own CO item, scope item and robot set; the
board links there rather than carrying a second copy of that linkage.

ChargeSplitSchema.description:
Charged value broken down by NetSuite status, for the coverage bar's
segments.

The segments sum to ``CoverageSchema.charged`` on a project with no
cancelled charges, and to less than it otherwise: ``charged`` mirrors the
project-overview widget, which counts cancelled rows, while the segments
exclude them. Treat them as a breakdown of what is live, not as a partition
of ``charged``.

CoverageSchema.description:
Value coverage — charged vs purchase-order, with the commercial offer as
context. Mirrors the project-overview "Overall value coverage" widget:
charged = Σ ServiceCharge (amount, or price·quantity); co = latest approved
offer's item total; po = Σ active purchase-order version amounts.
CoverageSchema.title: CoverageSchema

RollupSchema.description:
Per-project bespoke rollup, keyed by project id in the endpoint response.

Base project fields (code, owner, status, client, planned dates) are NOT
here — the frontend reads those from the shared core project-list endpoint
(``GET /api/core/v1/projects``) and merges this rollup in by id, so there is
a single source of truth for the project list.

empty); ``robot_sets`` is capped server-side (ROBOT_SET_LIMIT).
``turbines`` is finished against scoped turbines, absent when no live SOL
of the service names a turbine (see ``project_stats.sol_stats``).

CoveragePublishedPayload.description:
Payload WMS sends when a roster layer is published.

project_codes is the union of every project_code with at least one
assignment in the published layer's date range — WMS doesn't diff
against the prior snapshot. Our handler is idempotent so receiving
untouched codes is harmless. The ``Literal`` on ``event`` rejects
any other event type at the API boundary, before fan-out runs.

Uses plain ``ninja.Schema`` (not the ``extra='forbid'`` REST base) on
purpose: this is an inbound webhook from an external system, so unknown
fields WMS may add later are ignored rather than 422-rejected — the
integration stays forward-compatible without a lock-step deploy.
CoveragePublishedPayload.title: CoveragePublishedPayload

TaskUpdatedPayload.description:
Payload the travel app sends when one of its travel requests changes.

Uses plain ``ninja.Schema`` (not the ``extra='forbid'`` REST base) on
purpose: this is an inbound webhook from an external system, so unknown
fields the travel app may add later are ignored rather than 422-rejected —
the integration stays forward-compatible without a lock-step deploy.

Only ``project_code`` is consumed — it identifies which project to recompute
(the recompute re-reads the Travel API by project code). ``reference`` and
``event`` are accepted for logging/observability only.
TaskUpdatedPayload.title: TaskUpdatedPayload

AiAnomalyCoreSchema.description:
The ``core.anomaly`` columns registration writes that vis.ai_anomaly lacks.

A registration spans two tables, and until this existed the response showed
only the vis half — so a caller could not tell a column it never sent from
one the service dropped, and had to query the database to find out. Covers
the taxonomy cascade, the blade context resolved from
``service_order_line_id`` + ``component_name``, and the fields that are
derived when omitted (``name``, ``rib``).
AiAnomalyCoreSchema.title: AiAnomalyCoreSchema

AiAnomalySchema.description:
Response for a vis.AiAnomaly row — every column on the table.

``deleted_at`` is deliberately omitted (soft-delete internals are never
exposed); ``core_anomaly_id`` is the ``anomaly`` FK under its API name, and
``core_anomaly`` carries the half of the registration that lives on
``core.anomaly``.
AiAnomalySchema.title: AiAnomalySchema

AiAnomalyRegisterSchema.description:
Input for POST /vis/v1/ai-anomalies — the REST twin of registerAiDefect.

Field names and semantics mirror the GraphQL ``RegisterAiDefectInput``; both
surfaces feed the same ``vis.anomalies.register_ai_defect`` service.

Exactly one identifier must be supplied, matching internal_external:
``inference_defect_id`` for INTERNAL detections (they exist in the inference
pipeline) or ``defect_uid`` for EXTERNAL ones (they do not). BOTH accepts
either. This mirrors the vis.AiAnomaly CHECK constraints.

``component_name`` is the VIS blade name used to resolve the blade context.
The six ``*_component_id`` / ``*_type_id`` / ``material_id`` fields are the
anomaly taxonomy cascade and land on ``core.anomaly``. External detections
send none of them in practice, nor a ``qr_code`` or ``segmentation``. None
of that is enforced, and ``type_id`` / ``sub_type_id`` / ``material_id``
are accepted for externals.

``name`` and ``rib`` are optional because a caller need not know them:
omitted, they are derived from ``component_name`` or the blade section of
the ``source_object``. A supplied value wins.
AiAnomalyRegisterSchema.title: AiAnomalyRegisterSchema

AiAnomalyBulkResponseSchema.description: Output of POST /vis/v1/ai-anomalies/bulk, one result per item in input order.
AiAnomalyBulkResponseSchema.title: AiAnomalyBulkResponseSchema

AiAnomalyBulkRegisterSchema.description:
Input for POST /vis/v1/ai-anomalies/bulk: 1 to 200 registrations.

Each item is exactly the single-POST body. A malformed item (wrong type, an
unknown ``rib``) rejects the whole request with 422 before anything is
written; a business error (duplicate, unknown id) is reported per item.
AiAnomalyBulkRegisterSchema.title: AiAnomalyBulkRegisterSchema

AiAnomalySourceObjectSchema.description:
Input for PATCH /vis/v1/ai-anomalies/{id}/source-object.

The drone pipeline registers a defect before the portal has registered the
photo it came from, so the generic ``source_object`` pair is filled in once
that id exists.

A partial update: an omitted field is left untouched, while an explicit
``null`` clears that column. Patching one half of the pair never disturbs
the other, so the handler forwards presence rather than value.
AiAnomalySourceObjectSchema.title: AiAnomalySourceObjectSchema

no per-photo review state, and neither does a manual photo (rotation and sort
order only). ``MANUAL_PHOTO`` never appears on a submission: a manual photo
cannot carry anomalies.
